text:
ada: FYI — nightly dep-scan spike, ~18 transitive high/critical vulns across our node and rust deps. Seeing lot of crate/yarn churn. anyone else see this?
sec-bot: automated-alert: dependency-scan/nightly @eng: 18 findings (12 high, 6 critical). sample report: https://ci.redwood.example/reports/4938271600-deps.html :rotating_light:
olivia: ugh. could be noisy from the new infra-lib update. can you paste the top 3 CVEs?
mohit: top three: CVE-2025-4451, CVE-2026-1122, CVE-2024-9987 — two are transitive via pkgA -> pkgB. attaching small excerpt from the log: ```
/opt/ci/artifacts/sbom.json -> pkgB@1.4.2 -> vuln CVE-2025-4451 (high)
/opt/ci/artifacts/sbom.json -> pkgC@2.2.0 -> vuln CVE-2026-1122 (critical)
```
leo: quick triage Qs: 1) are these reproducible locally? 2) any commits from last 24h that bumped those deps?
jordan: reproduced `./tools/dep_scan --from=24h` locally and see same set. blame shows infra-lib bumped pkgB in pr #2412 yesterday.
nada: (typo, ignore)
ada2: (not a participant)
olivia: ok assign an owner. we should follow the standard evidence + ownership lifecycle: create security ticket, tag component owner, attach CI report, set severity, and block auto-merge until fix or documented mitigation.
mohit: assigning to @olivia as component owner for infra-lib? or to the last committer (ping @jordan)?
olivia: I'll take first-pass triage. plan: 1) verify exploitability and repro steps 2) check upstream fix / backport 3) consider temporary pin/patch 4) if no fix, create mitigation + runtime compensating control. target: triage within 24h. :thumbsup:
sec-bot: note: suppression requests require triage artifacts per policy: link https://docs.redwood.example/security/suppression-policy — must include repro, patch plan, and audit justification.
leo: KMS question: our dynamic scanner needs read access to private artifacts to generate SBOMs. we currently grant long-lived key to scanner SA; can we change to ephemeral KMS grants so audit logs show a short-lived grant for this run only?
olivia: yes — agreed we should avoid long-lived decrypt keys. @eng-infra, can you add a one-time ephemeral grant flow? we need audit events showing grant issuance and usage.
mohit: infra already prototyped `kms-ephemeral-grant` in staging. command: `kms-ephemeral-grant --service-account=scanner-sa --duration=15m --scope=artifacts:read` — it emits an audit event with grant_id. logs go to keystore-audit.
jordan: pinging infra: please prod this today for nightly runs. also add evidence retention flag so the SBOM and scanner output are attached to the security ticket (S3 path) and retained for 90 days for incident forensics.
olivia: adding to the ticket checklist: - attach SBOM + raw scanner output - include link to commit/PR that introduced bump - assign remediation owner - set embargo if PoC present
leo: on RBAC: if we change scanner SA permissions, we must update terraform module and run a TF plan; paging @eng-security to review before PROD roll.
mohit: agreed. add test in ci that fails if scanner SA has broad KMS decrypt role.
sec-bot: action-required: created ticket SEC-6123 with subject "dep-scan spike: infra-lib transitive vulns". ticket contains report: https://issues.redwood.example/SEC-6123
ada: small note on false positives: for quarantine rules we require at least 2 independent scanners (SAST/DAST or alternate dep scanner) before suppression. we only allow suppression when both mark FP and a human reviewer signs off.
olivia: good catch. will try reproduce with local SCA plus OSS index.
leo: incident response tie-in: if any of these are exploited in the wild we escalate to incident playbook A (page link https://runbook.redwood.example/security/incident-A). set incident_severity=high if exploitability confirmed.
jordan: I'll post a temporary PR to pin pkgB to 1.4.1 with a comment referencing SEC-6123 so we can unblock releases while upstream patch is evaluated.
mohit: ops: don't auto-merge that PR until infra confirms ephemeral KMS flows and auditlogs are in place — we need forensics preserved.
olivia: timeline recap: triage + repro by EOD, patch or mitigation PR within 48h, if not fixed escalate. I'll update SEC-6123 with findings. :white_check_mark:
sec-bot: reminder: retention policy enforced — artifacts for sec incidents auto-retained 90 days. audit trail id: grant-7c3a logged.
ada: thanks everyone. let's keep this thread updated with remediation links.
